Front, back and garage-entry door locks

faqs.q: Can you open my front door without damaging it?

faqs.q: Should I change my locks after moving in?
faqs.a: It is a common precaution because you cannot know who holds copies of the old keys. Rekeying is often a practical option when the existing locks are in good condition.

faqs.q: Do you install deadbolts?

intro: A business cannot afford a door that will not lock, or one that will not open. Commercial locks see heavier use than residential hardware, and a failed storefront or office door can stop the working day.
Locksmith Express MK provides mobile commercial locksmith assistance so repairs and rekeying can happen at your location, with minimal disruption to your team.
options: Panic bars and door hardware service
problems: An employee left and keys were not returned

faqs.q: What is a master key system?
faqs.a: A master key system lets different keys open different sets of locks, with a master key that opens all of them. It is commonly used in offices and multi-unit buildings.

faqs.q: Can you rekey the locks when an employee leaves?
faqs.a: Rekeying is a practical way to make a former employee's key stop working while keeping compatible existing lock hardware.

faqs.q: Do you work on glass storefront doors?
faqs.a: We service many commercial door locks. Contact us with details of your door and hardware so we can confirm what is possible.

intro: Locks do not last forever. Sticking cylinders, loose handles, rusted latches and damage from a break-in attempt are all signs that replacement may be a better answer than another repair.
Locksmith Express MK can assess your door and recommend hardware suited to how the property is used, then install it on site.
options: Front, side and back door locks
Replacing locks after a break-in attempt
Matching several locks to one key (where hardware allows)
problems: The lock is worn, loose or sticking
The door was forced or damaged
The hardware is outdated or low quality

authNote: We may ask for confirmation that you are the owner or an authorized agent before replacing locks on a property.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need a new lock?
faqs.a: Signs include a key that sticks or will not turn, a loose or damaged cylinder, rust, or hardware that was forced. A technician can assess it for you.

faqs.q: Can new locks use the same key?
faqs.a: Often several locks can be keyed alike, depending on the hardware. Ask us when you request a quote.

faqs.q: Is replacement or rekeying better?
faqs.a: Rekeying works for sound, compatible locks. Replacement suits worn, damaged or outdated hardware.

name: Lock Rekeying
card: Change which keys operate your existing locks without necessarily replacing the entire lock assembly.
subtitle: Make old keys stop working without necessarily replacing your lock hardware.
metaTitle: Lock Rekeying Service | Locksmith Express MK
metaDesc: Mobile lock rekeying for homes and businesses in Massachusetts and Connecticut. Change which keys work without replacing every lock.
intro: Rekeying changes the internal pins of a compatible lock so a new key operates it and the old keys do not. The lock stays on the door; only the key relationship changes.
It is a common choice after moving into a home, ending a tenancy, losing a key, or when staff leave a business. Locksmith Express MK performs rekeying at your location.
options: New keys cut for rekeyed locks
Rekeying after lost or stolen keys
problems: You just moved in and do not know who has keys
A key was lost or stolen
A tenant or employee left
You carry many keys and want fewer
suited: Anyone who wants old keys to stop working
authNote: We may ask for confirmation of ownership or authorization before rekeying locks on a property.

faqs.q: What is lock rekeying?
faqs.a: Rekeying changes the keys that operate an existing compatible lock, allowing you to retain the existing hardware while preventing the old keys from operating it.

faqs.q: Can every lock be rekeyed?
faqs.a: Many standard locks can be rekeyed, but not all. A technician will confirm compatibility.

faqs.q: Is rekeying cheaper than replacing?
faqs.a: It can be, depending on hardware and the number of locks. Pricing depends on the job, so request a quote.
